title: AdvHunter: Detecting Adversarial Perturbations in Black-Box Neural Networks through Hardware Performance Counters
problem: Adversarial examples can fool deep neural networks, and detecting them in black-box scenarios with only hard-label query access is challenging for proprietary DNNs deployed in practice.
motivation: Practical black-box adversarial detection is critical for securing deployed proprietary neural networks without requiring white-box access or retraining.
method: AdvHunter monitors hardware performance counters during DNN inference to capture microarchitectural data flow dynamics and applies Gaussian Mixture Models to detect anomalies indicative of adversarial examples in black-box settings.
key_novelty: Using hardware performance counters to detect adversarial perturbations in black-box neural networks without white-box access or model modification.
contributions: Black-box adversarial detection using hardware performance counter monitoring
Detection approach requiring only hard-label predictions without white-box model access
Gaussian Mixture Model-based anomaly detection from microarchitectural metrics
Evaluation across multiple datasets, architectures, and adversarial perturbation types

metrics.accuracy: detection rate and false positive rate

primary_theme: adversarial detection via hardware performance monitoring
